meta.title: Methodology | Diagnose, prioritize, and build
meta.description: The same team maps the problem, prioritizes what to solve, and builds the solution. No hand-offs, no reports nobody implements.

hero.title: Diagnose, prioritize, build — no hand-offs.
hero.subtitle: The same team runs the full cycle. Maps the ecosystem, surfaces the real problems, decides what to solve first, and builds it.
hero.intro: Most of the market splits into consultancies that deliver slide decks and disappear, or developers that execute without diagnostics. We sit in the empty space between the two: rigorous clarity in diagnosis and hands-on engineering in execution.

principles.title: 5 non-negotiable principles
principles.subtitle: The rules that hold every project together, regardless of which product.

items.title: Diagnostic before execution
items.body: We don't automate what we don't understand. Before building, we map the context, integrations, and critical dependencies.

items.title: No hand-offs
items.body: The team that diagnoses is the same one that builds. Information doesn't get lost between slide decks and briefings.

items.title: Decisions with explicit criteria
items.body: Every make / buy / consolidate recommendation is backed by impact, effort, risk, and estimated ROI. No theory.

items.title: No vendor lock-in
items.body: We recommend what fits, not what we get paid to resell. If your CRM works, we integrate. If it's broken, we say so first.

items.title: Editable deliverables
items.body: Reports, diagrams, and plans are yours in editable format. If you decide to execute internally or with another partner, you're not stuck with us.

pillars.title: Three connected stages, three standalone services
pillars.subtitle: You can start with any of them. Most companies start with the Digital X-Ray and move to the Roadmap or directly to Implementation.

items.title: Digital X-Ray
items.summary: We diagnose. Full inventory, integration map, risk analysis, and prioritized recommendations.

items.title: Technology Roadmap
items.summary: We prioritize. Target architecture, make/buy/consolidate decisions, estimated ROI, and phased plan in 4–6 weeks.

items.title: Implementation
items.summary: We build. AI automations, API integrations, dashboards, and custom systems. Fixed-scope project or monthly retainer.

flow.title: Diagnose → Prioritize → Build → Evolve
flow.subtitle: Each block delivers value on its own. Chained together, they transform the technology operation of the company.

steps.title: Diagnose
steps.body: Master inventory, license matrix, integration map, and risk analysis. Output: a real picture of the ecosystem.

steps.title: Prioritize
steps.body: Business vision, target architecture, make/buy/consolidate decisions, and phased plan with ROI. Output: an auditable roadmap.

steps.title: Build
steps.body: 1–2 week sprints with functional deliveries. Technical discovery, iterative build, controlled deployment. Output: capabilities in production.

steps.title: Evolve
steps.body: Monitoring, continuous improvement, new use cases. Automation isn't built and forgotten — it evolves with the business.

differentiator.title: Why this model doesn't exist in the market
differentiator.subtitle: The space between consultancies and developers is where most digital transformation projects die.

columns.title: Traditional consultancies
items: Charge premium for reports without execution
No responsibility over the final outcome

columns.title: IA Operators
items: Implementation in sprints with real deliveries

columns.title: AI / dev agencies
items: Build whatever you ask without diagnostics
Pretty demos that never reach production
No systemic view of the ecosystem
High risk of automating chaos on top of chaos

items.q: Do I have to contract all 3 products?
items.a: No. Each product delivers value on its own. You can run only the X-Ray, only the Roadmap, or jump straight into Implementation if you already know what to build.
Mid-sized companies usually start with the Digital X-Ray, move to the Roadmap when scope is large, and then contract Implementation as a fixed-scope project or retainer.
Both. Mid-market reality blends modern SaaS with legacy systems. The methodology works the same way in either context.

items.q: What size of company do you serve?
items.a: 50–500 people, revenue €2M–€100M. Sectors with high operational dependence on systems: hospitality, healthcare, professional services, retail, real estate, mid-market manufacturing.

items.q: Do you work alongside the in-house IT team?
items.a: Yes, ideally. The methodology is built with your team, not against it. CTO, IT Manager, and area owners participate in workshops and validate decisions.
